translation: Target defines a proposition (with no parameters or hypotheses) asserting the conjunction of five statements about Peano arithmetic (PA) and its set of theorems (PA.theory, i.e., the set of all arithmetic sentences derivable from PA in classical first-order logic): (1) there exists a recursively enumerable arithmetic theory F whose set of theorems equals PA.theory; (2) every sentence in PA.theory is true in the standard model of arithmetic (the natural numbers); (3) PA.theory, regarded as a set of axioms, is consistent (does not derive a contradiction in classical first-order logic); (4) the consistency sentence for PA.craig—namely, ¬Prov_{PA.craig}(⌜⊥⌝), built from the standard provability predicate of the Δ₁-presented theory PA.craig obtained by applying Craig's trick to PA (using PA's recursive enumerability)—is true in the standard model of arithmetic; and (5) that same consistency sentence ¬Prov_{PA.craig}(⌜⊥⌝) is not in PA.theory (i.e., is not derivable from PA).

divergences.description: Def7 PA defines the consistency sentence via Craig's trick (PA.craig.consistent.val) rather than directly using Peano arithmetic's canonical Δ₁ presentation, and Def6 PA.theory only existentially asserts that some recursively enumerable theory F has the same theorems as PA without explicitly tying that witness F to PA.craig. Since PA.craig has the same theorems as PA, its consistency sentence is still true in ℕ iff PA is consistent and is unprovable in PA, so this is a harmless technical artifact.

Chalmers's epistemic and cognitive notions—'our reasoning powers' being captured by a formal system, and being 'unable to see' or 'determine' consistency/soundness—cannot be directly expressed in the formal arithmetic setting and are idealized as membership in PA.theory (first-order provability from PA), with soundness specialized to truth in the standard model ℕ of first-order arithmetic.

Passage [P-C1b] refers to being unable to determine that F is sound, whereas Target only states that the consistency sentence is not among PA's theorems (matching [P-C1](c) and the author's claim, and in fact logically stronger as an unprovability claim than unprovability of soundness, though unprovability of soundness is not stated directly).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the claimed concrete instance (Peano arithmetic) of Chalmers's situation in [P-C1](c): PA's theorem set is recursively enumerable, sound in ℕ, and consistent, while its consistency sentence is true in ℕ yet unprovable in PA. Only minor caveats arise from using Craig's trick for the consistency sentence, idealizing epistemic notions as arithmetic provability, and focusing on unprovability of consistency rather than [P-C1b]'s wording about soundness.
